title: Rehoboam Rejects the Elders
text:
When King Solomon died, his son Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king. The people, led by Jeroboam, came to him with a request. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke on them with taxes and forced labor. If Rehoboam lightened it, they would serve him. He told them to come back in three days.

First he consulted the elders who had served his father. They advised him: if today you will be a servant to this people and answer them with kind words, they will be your servants forever.

Then he consulted the young men he had grown up with. They told him to answer: "My little finger is thicker than my father's loins. My father laid a heavy yoke on you, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."

Rehoboam followed the young men's advice and said exactly that. The people answered: "What share do we have in David? To your tents, O Israel!" When Rehoboam sent his official in charge of forced labor to them, they stoned him to death, and the king had to flee to Jerusalem in his chariot. Ten of the tribes made Jeroboam their king, and the kingdom was never united again.
lesson: When people ask you for relief, a show of toughness may feel strong but can break the very loyalty you rely on. Listen to experienced advisers, not just to the ones who tell you what you want to hear.
people: Rehoboam, the elders, the young advisers, Jeroboam, Adoram
